name: Gray Man

attributes.attribute: giant specter haunting Scottish and Irish shores
personifies the sea mist that drowns travelers
hunted boats carrying red-haired people or women
could attack any other boat on a whim

sources: Curran, Bob. *Complete Guide to Celtic Mythology.* Belfast: Appletree, 2000, 126-127.
Douglas, George. Scottish Fairy and Folk Tales. West Yorkshire: Ep Publishing, 1977, 94+.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Gray Man, also known as Far Liath or Liath Mhor, is a giant specter of Scottish and Irish coasts. He personifies the sea mist that swallows travelers and drowns them. He hunted especially for boats carrying red-haired people or women, yet he would attack any other boat on a whim. Curran and Douglas both record this folkloric figure.

okr.objective: Present the Gray Man as a sea-mist giant specter of Scotland and Ireland.
key_results: The Gray Man is a giant specter of Scottish and Irish coasts.
He personifies the sea mist in which travelers drown.
He sought boats with red-haired people or women.
Curran and Douglas both record the figure.
